neighbours.label: 'open' in the sense of free to share and reuse (open source, open licenses, open data), not physically open
fire: Many universities now publish their research in open access journals.
The developers released the game engine as an open source project on GitHub.
Our city launched an open data initiative so anyone can download the bus schedules.
Wikipedia relies on open licenses that let anyone reuse its articles.
The museum put its image collection under an Open Content program.
Linux is the best-known example of open source software in servers.
Researchers argued that open standards keep the web from being controlled by one firm.
The ministry will require that all funded textbooks use open licenses.
quiet: Many universities now publish their research in expensive printed journals.
The developers released the game engine after a long beta on GitHub.
Our city launched a new bus initiative so anyone can ride for less.
The janitor will open the gym doors at six every morning.
The museum keeps its image collection in a cool dark vault.
Linux runs on most servers in large data centers.
Researchers argued that the web is now controlled by a few big firms.
She left the window open so the kitchen would cool down.

predictions: Fires on ' open'/' Open' before source, access, license, data, standards; quiet on opening doors, boxes and shops.
notes: Probes: 'open source license' 0.87, 'open licenses' 0.34, 'Free and open software' 0.45, 'open data portal' 0.44, 'selfless' 0.27; 'open the door' 0.01, 'store is open' 0.005, 'opened the box' 0.004. A near miss with 'closed to outsiders' scored 0.27 on ' to', so 'closed' is avoided in near misses. The - pole's logit lens suppresses open/free/freedom.
